head_commit.message:
P-44's fix round: the group's first Run holds it, and the lane is held where the worlds queue

Muse, AGY (Flash) and a fresh Claude review of 0e06e2d.
- Muse: enqueue() cancelled any waiting Run, the one that holds the group among them when nothing
  was in progress, where GitHub would start it; nearly every cancellation on the seeds was that
  case. Now the group's first Run, in progress or waiting for a runner, holds it, and only a Run
  waiting behind it is cancelled. The cancellations fall from 68 seeds in 300 to 10 in the pull
  request's world. The empty lane is tested, and a mutant that drops the holder is killed.
- AGY and the review: the call sites were not held. Each world now checks that no more than one Run
  waits behind the one that holds the lane, a pinned seed of each world must show a cancellation,
  and mutants that queue past enqueue() are killed. The first seed whose Hold takes an item out of
  the queue is run as a pinned seed, so a run of forty seeds still asks for it.
- The design's rule is worded on what the port can see, a Run cancelled before its job had a runner
  or a step, names the test that holds it, says GitHub's pending is the records port's queued, and
  says a person's cancel reads the same, bounded by the Run ceiling. The superseded row's example
  names it. a_superseded_run_fails says a Run the Kernel refuses as it starts, and sim/AGENTS.md
  names the lane's test.
- The fixture's test ties each cancellation to the Run that replaced it, and holds the workflow's
  group to the blob the upload answered with.
AGY's major, that a cancelled Run spends an adjudication round, is the Kernel's reading of every
superseded Run today; it holds early, never late, and is not changed here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
CI: a Lens's verdict and the secret scan's rules run from the base (#145)

* CI: the secret scan's rules and verify's verdict are read from the base

"Run each deterministic Lens from the base's inputs" (issue 137), in the scope
the Maintainer shrank it to on 2026-10-17.

- ci.yml checks out the base under base/ (pull_request base SHA, the merge
  group's base_sha, or the pushed commit on a push) with the same pinned
  actions/checkout and persist-credentials: false. gitleaks reads
  --config base/.gitleaks.toml and --gitleaks-ignore-path base/.gitleaksignore,
  and the head's .gitleaksignore is deleted first: gitleaks 8.30.1 also reads
  <source>/.gitleaksignore whatever the flag says. EXEMPT gets the new hash.
- verify.yml's verify job checks out only the base and runs the base's
  tools/needs_passed.py. The example and the standard stay equal.
- check_workflows: a Lens job that judges its needs has one checkout, of the
  base and nothing else; scan_problems holds ci.yml to reading its rules from
  the base. Two tests with counter-cases, nine mutants.
- Decision 0023 records both, why no lens_inputs entry comes off the list, and
  ci.yml's further departure from the org's text. Design: P-37 for what
  merge_group.base_sha is for an entry behind another.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* CI: the secret scan reads every file as text and honours no inline allow

A fix round on "Run each deterministic Lens from the base's inputs" (issue 137),
from its review and security pass.

- ci.yml: gitleaks gets --log-opts="--full-history --all --diff-filter=tuxdb
  --text", its own 8.30.1 defaults plus --text, so a head's .gitattributes
  marking a file -diff cannot hide it as binary; and --ignore-gitleaks-allow,
  so an inline gitleaks:allow in head content passes over nothing. A local
  canary on gitleaks 8.30.1: the -diff file is missed with the default log
  options and caught with --text; the allowed line is caught only with the
  flag. scan_problems and the EXEMPT hash hold both.
- scan_problems strips quotes from a word, so bash -c "gitleaks ..." is read.
- _judging: a workflow with a judging job runs on pull_request and
  merge_group alone. On any other event ref: comes out empty and checkout
  takes the head without a word; the trigger is refused in the text, before
  any run, rather than given a fallback that fails at run time.
- Decision 0023 says what the base read buys whatever rules the base's
  configuration holds, and records the two flags and the trigger rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* CI: the secret scan's job is held step by step, not line by line

From the AGY review of "CI: the secret scan's rules and verify's verdict are
read from the base" (pull request 145).

- scan_problems held only the two lines around each gitleaks call, and the
  checkouts only in their order to each other: a `cp .gitleaks.toml base/`
  before the rm, or the base checkout moved after the scan, passed. It now
  holds the job whole: one job of four steps, in order, the head's checkout,
  the base's, an install that names no base and runs no gitleaks, and the
  scan, whose whole block is SCAN_RUN. No workflow-level or job-level env,
  defaults or container, no key on the scan step but name and run, and the
  install given only GITLEAKS_VERSION and GITLEAKS_CHECKSUM, so neither
  GIT_DIR nor a working-directory can move what the scan reads.
- Tests and mutants for the two branches that had none: a single-line run:
  read as a scan, and a judging workflow whose on: is a scalar.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* CI: one rule for the secret scan's command, and no code no test can reach

CI's mutation shards on pull request 145 reported four mutants as SURVIVED
that a local run had called killed: the reading of a gitleaks call by an
option, by a path, inside quotes, and the comparison of every call found with
SCAN_RUN. Run alone on an export, with gitleaks on PATH or off it, each
survives. Once the scan step's whole block had to equal SCAN_RUN and the job
had to be exactly four steps, that reading could change no verdict: a call
anywhere else is a fifth step, a changed block or an install line, all
refused already. The local kills were another test failing under a load
average near 30, which the harness counts as a kill.

- scan_problems: the hunt for gitleaks calls (SUBCOMMANDS, QUOTES,
  _runs_gitleaks) is gone. The rule is the job's shape and its last step's
  whole block equal to SCAN_RUN, with one message.
- Its mutants go with it; the comparison has two, false and the last line
  alone. A single-line run: is now held where it matters, an install on one
  line that names base/.
- Decision 0023's Boundary says the same.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
